$comment: Clause-level stack-side traceability for OPC UA WoT Binding and Projections:
it maps implemented behavior onto existing tests, with part-qualified
anchors for OPC 10101-2. It names the tests that hold that behavior, by
test name, so a reviewer can ask 'what proves this clause?' and get an answer
that a test run can check.
The statement-level map is wot-spec-requirements.json, which answers the
specification's own requirement identifiers. This file is the coarser view:
it names the tests that hold a whole clause, including the clauses the
specification does not leave to an implementation and so does not list there.
It is deliberately not a coverage report: a clause with tests here may still
be incompletely implemented. What it does guarantee is that every mapping
names a test that exists, is discoverable, and is not excluded from a normal
run - which is what WotBindingTraceabilityTests enforces, and what keeps a
renamed or deleted test from silently emptying a clause.
This is a stack-side test locator, not an authoritative copy of the current
specification text or a report of conformance to the official baseline.

clauses.title: Current-draft source-Thing receiver selection; not full published v1.00 interoperability
Ordinary TD/TM projection envelopes and result roles
Selection forms, precedence and local overrides
Provenance and owner-preserving closure; not full result schema validation

Organizational graph sharing and cycle rejection

Round-trip invariants for linked document sets
Notification data schema
Revision and conformance claims

Transmitted URI encoding
Binder and executor selection
EventType definitions and select clauses
Definitions named by logical identifier
Baseline derivation and explicit selection
Ordered definition sources and ambiguity

Default encodings and nested-only types
Engineering units

Published specification examples
Published OPC UA NodeId query grammar and conflict handling
clauses.evidence: Assertions pin canonical target identity and the complete endpoint path; numeric targets use the authored context. Duplicate decoded id query names throw FormatException rather than selecting one.

clauses.title: Full href and base-relative endpoint resource paths
clauses.evidence: Full and base-relative cases assert the exact endpoint BaseUri, target NodeId, scheme and host, including /UA/Plant/Line.

clauses.title: Reserved, percent, Unicode, and duplicate query handling
clauses.evidence: Transport tests pin UTF-8 escape sequences and unchanged ASCII. The Types supplement pins one-layer target decoding, escaped percent/hash/ampersand semantics and duplicate-query rejection.

clauses.title: Duplicate decoded target query names are rejected
clauses.evidence: Independent expected NodeId and endpoint literals detect over-decoding or endpoint-path loss; repeated decoded id names assert the exact rejection message.

clauses.title: Document-context numeric NodeId and action-owner mapping
clauses.evidence: Authored numeric indexes compile to the expected namespace URI despite different Session indexes; missing document authority produces no compiled form. Owner candidates retain their declared portable identities.

clauses.title: Document-context numeric browse prefixes and target validation
clauses.evidence: Tests pin mapped BrowseName namespace URIs and reject absent context or unselected published mode. Existing path executor tests reject incomplete/ambiguous targets and id/path disagreement before business services.

clauses.title: Explicit 1.00 selection and standard TD defaults
clauses.evidence: No-revision and revision cases assert explicit mode propagation; default selection remains Current. Standalone extraction compiles a context-mapped numeric path. Undefined modes reject the exact processingMode parameter.

clauses.title: Published property defaults, access flags, reads, and writes
clauses.evidence: Exact operation sets cover ordinary/readOnly/writeOnly/observable declarations. Live reads pin the typed value and namespace snapshot; writes translate caller indexes and verify the resulting upstream value in both modes.
clauses.qualification: TD access declarations do not confer Server permissions. Live service tests are not a complete access-control or reconnect campaign.

clauses.title: Native property observation and source namespace context
clauses.evidence: Published and Current cases receive the exact typed value through a live monitored item, assert Good status and an independent source namespace snapshot, and dispose the subscription.
clauses.qualification: This test pins initial observation and context, not a published-specific reconnect or cancellation fault campaign.

clauses.title: Action-level componentOf owner candidates
clauses.evidence: Tests assert candidate preservation, invalid/missing/scalar declarations, explicit-receiver membership and ambiguous-owner rejection. Successful dispatch assertions pin the actual ObjectId, not array position.

clauses.title: Live Method and receiver ownership preflight
clauses.evidence: Inherited ObjectType ownership accepts the containing Object; unrelated owners and endpoint mismatch reject before Call. Denied ownership browsing asserts the propagated status and zero business Calls.

clauses.title: Object-shaped schemas resolved by native argument order
clauses.evidence: Shuffled schema properties resolve to native argument names/order. Missing metadata prevents Call. Native Int32 rejects Int64 values on input and output. The live nested-owner acceptance returns the independent Float literal 3.5.

clauses.title: Argument and typed output agreement
clauses.evidence: Assertions pin native input/output vectors, reject wrong count/type/rank, retain required native arity despite optional/default JSON fields, and prevent partial output success or retry.

clauses.title: MIME admission separated from typed UA payload capability
clauses.evidence: The Call test observes typed Variants passed to the UA service. The codec test pins UTF-8 text bytes for a numeric value and exact ByteString decoding, explicitly distinguishing these from UA Binary serialization.
clauses.qualification: Partial capability, not full published serialization interoperability: no general UA Binary payload codec is implemented or claimed by this follow-up. MIME admission alone does not close that gap.

clauses.title: nosec channel selection and application policy
clauses.evidence: Explicit nosec planning asserts absence of invented channel constraints. Endpoint admission remains subject to the existing deployment policy; the TD cannot enable a disallowed channel.

clauses.title: Endpoint discovery and external identity credentials
clauses.evidence: Discovery tests reject endpoints with the wrong token kind and pin the selected compatible endpoint; exact constraints require a constraint-aware factory before connecting.
clauses.qualification: Credentials and endpoint policy remain external application/provider responsibilities. This is not evidence of every authentication provider or external identity service.

clauses.title: Exact channel, token, and allOf constraints
clauses.evidence: Published allOf asserts the retained mode, policy and token requirements together. Impossible combinations and unknown policies produce errors and no compiled form.

clauses.title: IssuedToken provider handoff
clauses.evidence: The configured constrained session factory receives the exact acquisition reference from the security requirement.
clauses.qualification: Provider handoff only: token acquisition and identity-provider interoperability require an application-supplied provider; no OAuth2 client or inline credential fallback is added.

clauses.title: Model declarations and runtime materialization boundaries
clauses.evidence: NodeSet serialization/read/import retains the registry document; generation activation rejects a required action without an executor instead of treating a declaration as executable.
clauses.qualification: Existing conversion/materialization boundaries, not complete TD/TM schema validation or whole-converter published equivalence.

clauses.title: Imported declarations retain names and scoped source metadata
clauses.evidence: A genuine resolver closure survives conversion and NodeSet import into planning with the original owner. Forged resolvedFrom JSON, even with an authored owner array, cannot supply trusted source authority; local identity is asserted separately.

clauses.title: Property-scoped protocol-neutral target mapping
clauses.evidence: Tests pin extracted and compiled node/type/field mapping values and reject form-level or non-property placement with the expected diagnostic.
clauses.qualification: These are mapping-contract assertions, not evidence of every protocol's live value-to-structured-field execution.

clauses.title: The authorized Method and receiver are the dispatched pair
clauses.evidence: Successful calls assert the actual receiver and Method; denied preflight asserts zero Calls. The MCP supplement checks grants and dispatched pair against the same captured identities.

clauses.title: MCP authorization and dispatch use the same published owner candidate
clauses.evidence: Positive MCP execution pins authorization and service ObjectId/MethodId. Denied receiver fails Open with BadUserAccessDenied and issues no Call.

clauses.title: Original source owner evidence across import and projection
clauses.evidence: Resolver tests pin the original action/owner identities rather than the projection root; capture rejects unresolved/forged provenance. The MODEL-02 supplement exercises the live resolver and NodeSet import seam.

clauses.title: Generation-bounded channel and target authority
clauses.evidence: Session identity mutation during ownership browsing fails without Call; invalid path targets issue no business Read. Metadata remains operation-local rather than a cross-generation global cache.

clauses.title: No published UA event mapping; current event regression only
clauses.qualification: Not a published v1.00 requirement. Existing event identity/selection tests remain regression evidence only; no eventFields format is introduced.

clauses.title: Part-version-qualified evidence and conformance qualifications
clauses.qualification: The ledger verifies test locators, not clause completeness, coverage percentages, CTT or certification. Complete TD/TM/Binding-result schema validation remains blocked separately.
